record.context_brief: From auxiliary Krylov solvability to standard Krylov solvability
record.original_question: Assume (A0, A~0) is a joint pair of abstract Friedrichs operators on a Hilbert space H, meaning that A0 and A~0 are closed and densely defined, A0 is contained in (A~0)* =: A1, A~0 is contained in (A0)* =: A~1, and A1 + A~1 is a bounded self-adjoint operator with strictly positive bottom. Suppose further that the hypotheses g ∈ ran A ∩ dom A* and A* g ∈ Dqa(A* A) hold in a way that yields a unique solution of the auxiliary problem A* A f = A* g lying in K(A* A, A* g). What additional assumptions are needed to upgrade this auxiliary Krylov solvability to standard Krylov solvability of Af = g for a chosen closed realization (A, A*) of (A0, A~0), that is, to ensure the solution belongs to K(A, g)?

evidence.quote: This way one naturally comes to the definition of a joint pair of abstract Friedrichs operators on a complex Hilbert space H as a pair (A0, A~0) of two closed and densely defined operators acting in H and satisfying the conditions A0 ⊂ (A~0)* =: A1 , A~0 ⊂ (A0)* =: A~1 , A1 + A~1 is a bounded self-adjoint operator in H with strictly positive bottom.

Here A* A is self-adjoint (see, e.g., [38, Theorem 12.11]), and A* g ∈ ran A* A ∩ Dqa(A* A). These are precisely the conditions that allow to deduce, via Theorem 2.7, that there exists a unique solution f ∈ K(A* A, A* g) to the inverse problem (4.2).

QUESTION 2: Assume that (A0, A~0) is a joint pair of abstract Friedrichs operators on H satisfying (4.1) and hence such that there is a unique solution f to A0 f = g belonging to K(A*0 A0, A*0 g). What assumptions need be added in order to obtain the standard Krylov solvability of Af = g, where (A, A*) is one of the closed realisations of (A0, A~0) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a complex Hilbert space. A joint pair of abstract Friedrichs operators on H is a pair (A_0, Ã_0) of closed, densely defined linear operators on H satisfying:
(i) A_0 ⊂ (Ã_0)* =: A_1,
(ii) Ã_0 ⊂ (A_0)* =: Ã_1,
(iii) A_1 + Ã_1 is a bounded self-adjoint operator on H whose spectrum is bounded below by a strictly positive constant.

A closed realisation of (A_0, Ã_0) is any pair (A, A*) of mutually adjoint closed operators with A_0 ⊂ A ⊂ A_1 (equivalently Ã_0 ⊂ A* ⊂ Ã_1).

For a closed densely defined operator T on H and a vector v ∈ H with v ∈ ⋂_{n≥0} dom(T^n), define the Krylov subspace
K(T, v) := span{ T^n v : n = 0, 1, 2, … },
and write its closure as K(T, v)‾. For a self-adjoint operator S, let D_qa(S) := ⋂_{n≥0} dom(S^n) (the space of quasi-analytic-type vectors on which all powers act).

Fix a closed realisation (A, A*) of (A_0, Ã_0) and let g ∈ H. Assume:
(a) g ∈ ran(A) ∩ dom(A*),
(b) A*g ∈ D_qa(A*A),
so that the self-adjoint operator A*A and the vector A*g satisfy the hypotheses guaranteeing existence and uniqueness of a solution f ∈ K(A*A, A*g)‾ to the auxiliary normal-equation problem
A*A f = A*g.
This f is automatically also a solution of Af = g.

Problem. Determine additional assumptions on (A_0, Ã_0), on the chosen closed realisation (A, A*), and/or on g, under which the uniquely determined solution f above belongs to the standard Krylov subspace K(A, g)‾; that is, find conditions that upgrade auxiliary Krylov solvability (f ∈ K(A*A, A*g)‾) to standard Krylov solvability (f ∈ K(A, g)‾) of the inverse problem Af = g.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2024 work surveying open problems and perspectives on Krylov approximation for Friedrichs systems. No subsequent paper resolving it was found; related recent work (2024–2025) on Krylov solvability for unbounded self-adjoint operators and Friedrichs systems on an interval does not address the auxiliary-to-standard upgrade in this generality.
